findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing or unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or handle with map_err

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value in parts[1]
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (e.g., alphabetic text in the value column) causes a panic instead of a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(...) and propagate as a Result type, or parse directly into u16 with range-checked result

findings.problem: Lossy as cast (.parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16) silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value in range 65536..=u32::MAX wraps to a wrong u16 silently, producing data corruption without any error indication
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) or parse directly to u16 and propagate the TryFromError

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing on split result
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields triggers a panic at runtime via out-of-bounds slice access
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') and handle the None case with a typed error, or use .get(0) with Option handling

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing on split result
findings.failure_mode: a line with only one field (no comma) triggers a panic at runtime via out-of-bounds slice access on parts[1]
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get name/value pair, or .get(1) with Option and map to a typed error

findings.problem: split(',').map().collect() to extract two fields instead of split_once
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation of Vec<String> for every line, plus O(n) field scanning when only two delimited fields are needed
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name_part, value_part) directly without Vec allocation

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is hidden I/O side effect in a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: side-effecting I/O in what appears to be a pure data-loading function makes the function non-deterministic, untestable, and violates functional core / imperative shell separation. The side effect is also a hidden observable behavior not documented in the function signature.
findings.fix: remove println! entirely, or return a side-channel (e.g., a mutable log Vec or callback) if audit logging is required. The pure core must contain zero I/O.

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println!), and data parsing in a single public function
findings.failure_mode: the entire pipeline is untestable as pure logic. File I/O, parsing, and side effects are entangled, making unit testing impossible without filesystem setup and producing non-deterministic output from println!
findings.fix: split into: (1) shell: fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that reads and delegates, (2) core: fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that contains zero I/O

findings.problem: Vec<String> allocation for every line just to split two comma-separated fields
findings.failure_mode: excessive heap allocation per line. For a file with N lines, this allocates N Vec<String> objects plus N individual String allocations for trimmed parts, when split_once + &str would avoid all of them.
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to borrow &str fragments directly, trim and clone only the final two fields needed for Record construction

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() as u16: width change via as after parse instead of try_from
findings.failure_mode: any parsed value > 65535 silently truncates, losing data integrity. The Holzman rule mandates try_from for all width changes.
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and propagate the error, or parse directly to u16 via .parse::<u16>()

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_sessions
findings.failure_mode: without benchmarks or allocation tracking, the O(N) Vec allocation pattern per line and overall throughput characteristics are unmeasured. Performance claims cannot be validated.
findings.fix: add a benchmark using criterion or similar, and allocation tracking with dhat or similar to verify the allocation profile of the parsing path

findings.problem: No dev-dependencies for testing, benchmarks, or CI evidence tooling
findings.failure_mode: no test framework, benchmarking harness, or lint tooling declared. The Holzman review process requires command evidence (cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo fmt) to validate compliance.
findings.fix: add criterion as dev-dependency for benchmarks, and ensure CI runs cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, and cargo test

residual_risk: This crate has 10 BLOCKER findings and 2 MEDIUM findings across zero_forbidden_constructs, parsing, functional_core_imperative_shell, allocation, and conversions rules. The code is fundamentally non-compliant: every parse path uses unwrap or as casts, I/O is mixed with data logic, and all indexed slice access is unchecked. No commands were run (static review only); actual runtime failure points are certain given malformed input.
